regional_command.description: The Baath's Regional Command must turn a movement built for conspiracy into an organization capable of governing Iraq. Its appointments will shape the relationship between the party, the ministries and the officers on whom the republic still depends.
regional_command.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
regional_command.rationale: Organized appointments strengthen command and reduce officer-selection costs; not a redundant party-access unlock.

national_front.description: The Communists and other organized forces possess expertise that the Baath cannot simply command into existence. A national front could put that experience to work, provided its partners receive guarantees that mean more than a place on the government's letterhead.
national_front.reference: IRQ_ministry_of_education/IRQ_restructure_school_curriculum (05_iraq.txt): real education law and education-cost/research spirit. 1970 adaptation uses education costs/literacy or bounded categories.
national_front.rationale: Conditional accepted coalition brings organized labour and civilian expertise; its contract gate remains mandatory. Replace universal research with actual educational administration.

baath_monopoly.description: The party can reserve the commanding offices of the Iraqi state for its own members. A single chain of authority will make decisions easier to enforce, although those excluded from public life will take some of their knowledge and cooperation with them.
baath_monopoly.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
baath_monopoly.rationale: Executive mobilisation is useful without the Front's industrial/educational participation; exclusion costs expertise.

front_guarantees.description: A signature in Baghdad will not settle every dispute between the Front's parties. Ministers, workplace representatives and provincial organizers need enforceable rules if cooperation is to survive the first serious disagreement over appointments or public money.
front_guarantees.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
front_guarantees.rationale: An upheld coalition charter reduces exceptional security administration; benefits require the existing accepted Front contract.

party_screening.description: Our ministries and armed forces contain men whose loyalties reach beyond the Regional Command. Screening appointments will strengthen the leadership's access to information and trusted officers, but political reliability cannot replace professional competence in every post.
party_screening.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
party_screening.rationale: Political screening offers information and cheaper trusted appointments but reduces merit; it is not a free purges bonus.

baath_congress.description: A regional congress can bind the party's provincial organizations to a common programme rather than a collection of personal promises. It must also provide a recognized forum for the leadership disputes that otherwise spread through the ministries and barracks.
baath_congress.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
baath_congress.rationale: A governing congress also organizes civilian offices; the succession decision is additional, not the whole reward.

mass_party.description: Workers, students and rural organizers can give the Baath a presence far beyond its original circles. Bringing them into a mass movement will deepen the state's reach, while making employment, services and material support matters of party responsibility.
mass_party.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
mass_party.rationale: Mass organizations mobilize reserves and carry real social obligations; they do not spawn free divisions.

cadre_party.description: A smaller party can devote more attention to the training and discipline of its organizers. Iraq would gain a more practiced governing core, but it would have fewer people able to carry the party's demands into every town and village.
cadre_party.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
cadre_party.rationale: A smaller trained apparatus improves initial production organization while reaching fewer recruits.

popular_organizations.description: The party's associations must offer something to the families they seek to organize. Medical assistance and public services can give these bodies a lasting place in Iraqi society, provided Baghdad accepts the obligations that accompany that influence.
popular_organizations.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
popular_organizations.rationale: Public associations deliver health/logistical services alongside political mobilization; social commitments cost money.

party_schools.description: Party schools can prepare provincial organizers for work more demanding than repeating instructions from Baghdad. Technical lessons and administrative training will help them manage public undertakings, although the government must distinguish useful instruction from political ritual.

party_schools.rationale: Cadre instruction delivers one concrete industrial course plus lower educational administration costs.

baath_accounts.description: The boundary between a party undertaking and a public enterprise has become dangerously uncertain. Separate accounts will make Iraqi revenues easier to collect and contracts easier to supervise, while limiting the discretion of officials accustomed to treating both treasuries as their own.
baath_accounts.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
baath_accounts.rationale: Separating enterprise and party accounts improves actual corporate collection, at a political-control cost.

arab_socialism.description: Iraq's public sector is expected to carry much of the country's industrial transformation. Giving it a stronger productive foundation will support that ambition, but investment directed through the state leaves fewer resources available for immediate private consumption.
arab_socialism.reference: IRQ_state_sponsored_industries/IRQ_revive_damaged_companies (05_iraq.txt): civilian plant delivery and +15% civilian construction spirit; no paid generic helper copied.
arab_socialism.rationale: The state-sector commitment raises civilian productivity and production depth, while reserving more civilian resources.

secular_state.description: Public offices must serve Iraq's citizens through a common set of procedures. Reducing competing religious and personal channels of authority can make administration more dependable, even where the party finds that professional officials are less willing to follow informal instructions.
secular_state.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
secular_state.rationale: A common state service reduces duplicative administrative and sectarian security offices, with less party control.

women_unions.description: Iraqi women cannot contribute fully to public life while training and paid employment remain closed to them. The unions and ministries can widen those opportunities, but employment must be supported by services that allow families to sustain the change.
women_unions.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
women_unions.rationale: Qualified employment strengthens civilian production rather than an unexplained national research bonus.

enterprise_accounts.description: Public enterprises need accounts that reveal whether workshops are producing useful goods or merely satisfying a minister's report. Regular inspection will help managers coordinate production and collection, while adding responsibilities that neither the ministry nor the enterprise can evade.
enterprise_accounts.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
enterprise_accounts.rationale: Audited state contracts improve collection and factory coordination; audit overhead is explicit.

baath_citizenship.description: The republic cannot govern indefinitely through separate bargains with every community and local notable. A common citizenship would make public responsibilities more predictable, although officials will have to surrender some of the informal leverage on which party control has relied.
baath_citizenship.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
baath_citizenship.rationale: Common citizenship reduces exceptional policing and vulnerability to outside political sponsors; it does not automatically settle Kurdish autonomy.

party_social_bargain.description: The party asks Iraqi households to place development ahead of immediate comfort. A credible bargain must offer dependable education and medical care in return, and those commitments must remain in the budget after the speeches have ended.
party_social_bargain.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
party_social_bargain.rationale: An actual household-service budget replaces stability points lost at the common cap.

baath_future.description: The Baathist republic must outlast individual campaigns and the men who announce them. A governing apparatus able to organize technical instruction, public offices and industrial work would give the party a stronger foundation than personal loyalty alone.

baath_future.rationale: The capstone institutionalizes production and administration; it retains one bounded industrial-training delivery.

bakr_presidency.description: Al-Bakr stands at the meeting point of the party and the military networks that helped bring it to power. His presidency can use those connections to staff the republic, but maintaining their cooperation will require more than issuing orders from Baghdad.
bakr_presidency.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
bakr_presidency.rationale: Bakr's military/party networks support appointments; his office gate remains unchanged.

bakr_collective.description: Al-Bakr can give experienced colleagues a greater share in the daily work of government. Collective leadership would draw on a wider pool of expertise, while obliging the presidency to negotiate decisions that a narrower executive might impose.
bakr_collective.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
bakr_collective.rationale: Collective government offers competent shared administration at slower executive decision-making.

bakr_presidential.description: The president can make himself the final arbiter between competing party offices and commanders. That authority promises a clearer direction for Iraq, but the organizations that accept his arbitration will expect their own positions to be maintained.
bakr_presidential.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
bakr_presidential.rationale: Presidential arbitration offers command and political capacity, with continuing patronage commitments.

bakr_council.description: The Command Council must do more than ratify decisions already reached elsewhere. A regular division of military and educational responsibilities could make it useful to the republic, provided its members accept procedures that restrain personal intervention.
bakr_council.reference: IRQ_ministry_of_education/IRQ_restructure_school_curriculum (05_iraq.txt): real education law and education-cost/research spirit. 1970 adaptation uses education costs/literacy or bounded categories.
bakr_council.rationale: Council government supports trained officers and public instruction rather than a second bureaucracy-only reward.

bakr_loyal_officers.description: Al-Bakr's standing among experienced officers is an important part of his authority. Giving trusted men a recognized role in training and mobilization can strengthen the presidency, although too narrow a circle would close the army to other capable officers.
bakr_loyal_officers.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
bakr_loyal_officers.rationale: Trusted officers deliver mobilization and training, with reduced openness to expertise.

bakr_continuity.description: The presidency needs a secretariat that keeps ministries working when senior officials are occupied with party affairs. Reliable records and a settled division of responsibilities will make the state's ordinary business less dependent on the president's personal attention.
bakr_continuity.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
bakr_continuity.rationale: A working secretariat improves household tax collection and routine administration.

bakr_contain_deputy.description: The deputy's expanding responsibilities have made the division of authority increasingly uncertain. Al-Bakr can seek a clearer settlement of offices, but effective scrutiny will also limit the freedom of the presidency itself.
bakr_contain_deputy.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
bakr_contain_deputy.rationale: A division of offices creates institutional scrutiny rather than another capped stability payment; succession remains negotiated.

bakr_delegate.description: Saddam has demonstrated an ability to pursue decisions through the party apparatus. Delegating more of the government's work to him may accelerate development, while placing a larger security and administrative machine under the deputy's influence.
bakr_delegate.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
bakr_delegate.rationale: Delegated executive coordination can deliver development quickly but expands the security apparatus.

bakr_guarantees.description: The officers and party veterans who sustain the presidency fear being displaced by a new executive circle. A recognized place for them can make the governing establishment more dependable, at the price of restricting future appointments and reforms.
bakr_guarantees.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
bakr_guarantees.rationale: An agreed old-guard establishment stabilizes appointments and payroll, limiting executive freedom.

bakr_deputy_budget.description: Development orders pass through too many offices before reaching the people expected to carry them out. A coordinating budget under the deputy could connect public projects with responsible officials, although their cooperation will require concessions from the treasury.
bakr_deputy_budget.reference: IRQ_state_sponsored_industries/IRQ_revive_damaged_companies (05_iraq.txt): civilian plant delivery and +15% civilian construction spirit; no paid generic helper copied.
bakr_deputy_budget.rationale: The deputy's implementation office delivers projects but grants concessions to those executing them.

bakr_development.description: The capital's industrial ambitions depend on roads and public works that can carry materials as well as official delegations. A funded programme around Baghdad will give al-Bakr's development policy a practical foundation that survives changes in the cabinet.
bakr_development.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
bakr_development.rationale: A funded infrastructure priority leaves a physical Baghdad project rather than only two-percent construction.

bakr_treaty.description: Closer relations with Moscow could provide Iraq with military and technical opportunities. Our own officers must first prepare the stores, training arrangements and negotiating positions needed to use any agreement; Soviet cooperation will still depend on Soviet decisions.
bakr_treaty.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
bakr_treaty.rationale: Iraqi reception/logistics preparation has a domestic payoff even if Moscow declines the separate treaty; no Soviet arms are conjured.

bakr_north.description: A northern guarantee will be judged by the services and conduct of the state, rather than the wording of a communiqué. Al-Bakr must prepare civilian institutions capable of carrying out promises that can otherwise be undone by a local security office.
bakr_north.reference: IRQ_ministry_of_education/IRQ_restructure_school_curriculum (05_iraq.txt): real education law and education-cost/research spirit. 1970 adaptation uses education costs/literacy or bounded categories.
bakr_north.rationale: Preparing northern public guarantees changes services and exceptional security costs; it does not bypass the accepted-settlement system.

bakr_unity.description: A conference with Syria would bring rival claims to Arab leadership into the same room. Iraq needs officials able to examine common projects and responsibilities before asking Damascus to accept a union whose institutions neither side has yet defined.
bakr_unity.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
bakr_unity.rationale: Iraq's own joint-planning staff becomes useful before a separately consensual Syrian union conference.

bakr_technical_mission.description: Iraq can purchase machinery more quickly than it can train the people needed to operate it. Technical missions must therefore build Iraqi engineering and construction knowledge, so that development does not depend indefinitely on specialists recalled by another government.

bakr_compromise.description: Al-Bakr's presidency rests on institutions whose interests do not always coincide. A durable compromise would give them dependable civilian channels for their work, while requiring the leadership to accept limits that cannot be withdrawn at the first disagreement.
bakr_compromise.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
bakr_compromise.rationale: A workable institutional settlement improves civil administration instead of another stability-only compromise.

bakr_union_charter.description: Arab cooperation needs rules for contracts and public revenue as well as declarations of fraternity. A charter can make Iraqi undertakings easier for partners to understand, without committing Syria or any other government to arrangements it has not accepted.
bakr_union_charter.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
bakr_union_charter.rationale: Standard public contract terms support external commerce; the charter does not annex Syria or force an investment.

bakr_succession_plan.description: The presidency should pass through an agreement that the republic's institutions can recognize. Al-Bakr must settle the authority of an eligible successor with those whose cooperation will determine whether government continues to function after his departure.
bakr_succession_plan.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
bakr_succession_plan.rationale: A short genuine political gateway: institutional continuity remains while the incumbent governs; transition still requires the real succession decision.

saddam_presidency.description: Saddam's rise from the party apparatus to the presidency will change the balance between civilian organizers and the military establishment. He must turn control over competing offices into a government capable of acting, while confronting the distrust that such concentration of power creates.
saddam_presidency.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
saddam_presidency.rationale: The presidency delivers executive command with immediate political strain; no free government change.

saddam_personal_state.description: The presidency can bring rival offices into a chain of authority centered on Saddam himself. A personal executive will receive information and issue decisions more quickly, but it must sustain the security organizations on which that authority rests.
saddam_personal_state.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
saddam_personal_state.rationale: A personal executive gains information and rapid decisions while sustaining expensive exceptional security.

saddam_party_cabinet.description: A cabinet of established party officials and specialists can give the presidency a broader administrative base. Keeping their expertise in public service will require room for professional judgment that a fully personal executive would find uncomfortable.
saddam_party_cabinet.reference: IRQ_ministry_of_education/IRQ_restructure_school_curriculum (05_iraq.txt): real education law and education-cost/research spirit. 1970 adaptation uses education costs/literacy or bounded categories.
saddam_party_cabinet.rationale: The party cabinet offers civilian expertise and cheaper education rather than the personal state's coercive reach.

saddam_security_bureau.description: The presidency needs dependable information about the military, the party and foreign interference in Iraq. A stronger security bureau can supply it, but overlapping surveillance and exceptional powers will burden both the public treasury and relations within the state.
saddam_security_bureau.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
saddam_security_bureau.rationale: Domestic information and counter-interference are tangible; security expansion retains genuine expense and strain.

saddam_technocrats.description: Experienced managers understand problems that cannot be solved by replacing an official with a more loyal party member. Retaining them will improve industrial administration, while limiting the presidency's freedom to use every appointment as a political reward.
saddam_technocrats.reference: IRQ_state_sponsored_industries/IRQ_revive_damaged_companies (05_iraq.txt): civilian plant delivery and +15% civilian construction spirit; no paid generic helper copied.
saddam_technocrats.rationale: Retained specialists improve production organization while restricting political appointments.

saddam_social_contract.description: Oil receipts allow the government to promise Iraqi households a better material life. Medical provision and access to consumer goods can support the presidency's claim to govern for development, provided these commitments remain affordable when revenues or military demands change.
saddam_social_contract.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
saddam_social_contract.rationale: Oil finances household services and consumption; the public welfare commitment stays on the budget.

saddam_guard.description: A presidential guard gives the leadership formations whose readiness and loyalty can be cultivated closely. Preferential training and dependable stores can strengthen the regime's military position, but maintaining that standard places a lasting burden on the army's payroll.
saddam_guard.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
saddam_guard.rationale: Keep the approved Guard trade-off; national abstraction, no selective elite-unit claim.

saddam_regular_army.description: Iraq's military strength cannot rest on privileged formations alone. Investment in the regular army's training and replacement system will give its commanders more dependable forces, while committing the government to a broader permanent establishment.
saddam_regular_army.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
saddam_regular_army.rationale: Keep the approved regular-army alternative; broader training/recovery instead of Guard cohesion.

saddam_guard_supply.description: Favored formations cannot maintain their readiness on political standing alone. Common stores and practical equipment work will support the Guard's place in the army, although privileged supply arrangements must still be staffed and paid for.
saddam_guard_supply.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
saddam_guard_supply.rationale: Privileged stores and common upgrades have a concrete logistics payoff and continuing pay burden.

saddam_staff_college.description: The presidency needs officers who can coordinate formations rather than merely command their own battalions. Staff appointments should therefore be supported by serious instruction, even where a trained commander proves less dependent on political supervision.
saddam_staff_college.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
saddam_staff_college.rationale: Staff appointments produce actual finite military experience and trained-command capability.

saddam_regional_role.description: Iraq's ambitions in the Arab world require a government able to negotiate and sustain military purchases. A more capable diplomatic and procurement service can widen Baghdad's options, while leaving foreign suppliers and neighboring governments free to defend their own interests.
saddam_regional_role.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
saddam_regional_role.rationale: Regional influence and arms procurement are actual capabilities; foreign governments still decide whether to cooperate.

saddam_iran_dossier.description: Events in Iran may alter the regional balance without revealing how its armed forces would perform in a war. Iraqi planners need a sober assessment of command and supply before the presidency treats apparent disorder across the frontier as an opportunity.
saddam_iran_dossier.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
saddam_iran_dossier.rationale: An Iraqi operational assessment delivers planning experience, not an automatic Iranian revolution or war.

saddam_industry.description: Presidential projects must leave Iraq with useful production rather than monuments to the officials who commissioned them. A civilian plant in Baghdad can support the wider industrial programme, although its construction will compete with immediate household demands.
saddam_industry.reference: IRQ_state_sponsored_industries/IRQ_revive_damaged_companies (05_iraq.txt): civilian plant delivery and +15% civilian construction spirit; no paid generic helper copied.
saddam_industry.rationale: Preserve the existing paid Baghdad plant and add domestic industrial capacity; no free helper.

saddam_credit.description: A foreign credit line will be easier to negotiate if Baghdad can present accounts that creditors understand. The same work can strengthen domestic collection, while the terms and availability of any Gulf loan remain matters for the lender to decide.
saddam_credit.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
saddam_credit.rationale: The credit office also improves domestic accounts; real foreign credit remains matched lender money and Iraqi debt.

saddam_bounded_deterrence.description: A credible deterrent needs forces able to mobilize and defend Iraqi territory. The presidency can sustain that preparation without treating every frontier dispute as an instruction to begin a war, but readiness will still carry a standing personnel bill.
saddam_bounded_deterrence.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
saddam_bounded_deterrence.rationale: Deterrence buys real defensive preparedness without a fabricated casus belli.

saddam_local_procurement.description: Imported equipment is only useful while Iraq can maintain and replace its essential parts. Domestic workshops and a more practiced licensing service will reduce exposure to shortages, without pretending that every foreign design can be reproduced at once.
saddam_local_procurement.reference: IRQ_state_sponsored_industries/IRQ_revive_damaged_companies (05_iraq.txt): civilian plant delivery and +15% civilian construction spirit; no paid generic helper copied.
saddam_local_procurement.rationale: Domestic repair and licensed manufacture reduce shortage exposure rather than an unexplained research gain.

saddam_debt_service.description: The political value of a credit agreement fades when its repayments fall due. Baghdad needs a revenue authority able to meet obligations without concealing their burden, and creditors must retain the claims they have actually agreed to hold.
saddam_debt_service.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
saddam_debt_service.rationale: A financed repayment authority collects revenue with public strain; no focus cancels debt or transfers creditor assets.

saddam_legacy.description: The presidency must turn personal loyalties and competing offices into an administration that can carry out its decisions. A clearer executive chain will reduce duplicated work, while concessions to the institutions sustaining the regime narrow the state's revenue base.
saddam_legacy.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
saddam_legacy.rationale: Executive continuity retains a real tax concession and stronger civil institutions; do not stack Bakr's inactive office.

officer_council.description: An officer government inherits more than the command of the armed forces. Its members must establish authority over a fractured political system without assuming that the methods of the barracks will command the same confidence in civilian life.

officer_council.rationale: The officer council has concrete command capacity and remains a genuinely contested government.

officer_garrisons.description: Provincial commanders possess the forces to enforce orders where civilian administration is weak. A garrison government can use that presence to support collection and policing, but soldiers assigned to such duties remain an expensive substitute for ordinary public offices.

Trusted networks can accelerate mobilization and decisions, but personal confidence is a poor substitute for the cohesion that competent leadership builds within a formation.

officer_logistics.description: Different commands cannot sustain themselves indefinitely through separate stores and purchasing arrangements. officer_continuity.description: A future cabinet needs confidence that routine government will continue when the armed forces return to their military duties. Civilian guarantees can reduce exceptional policing and outside political leverage without allowing the council to choose every successor government.

officer_settlement.description: Iraq needs an enduring division between military command and civilian authority rather than another temporary balance of personalities. A recognized establishment will make the army more coherent, but its service and responsibilities must be carried honestly in the budget.

arab_republican_movement.description: Iraqi Arab socialists must reconcile their commitment to Arab cooperation with the institutions required to govern their own country. arab_iraqi_sovereignty.description: An Arab republic need not surrender Iraqi decision-making to another capital. arab_joint_planning.description: Arab development schemes will fail if participating governments cannot identify who supplies the money, materials and administration. arab_public_service.description: Republican service must offer careers based on the work Iraq needs done. A professional administration can connect public decisions with productive activity, provided ministries are staffed for competence rather than divided among the sponsors of the latest cabinet.

arab_state_contracts.description: A public industrial contract should leave Iraq with an operating plant rather than another office responsible for supervising one. arab_palestine.description: Solidarity with the Palestinians requires an administration able to sustain the commitments Baghdad actually makes. arab_technical_exchange.description: Iraq needs technical exchanges that leave knowledge in its own workshops and construction offices. Training engineers to adapt what they learn abroad will make development less dependent on the continuing presence of a foreign mission.

arab_civil_diplomacy.description: Arab cooperation can be advanced through civilian projects and commercial undertakings as well as political declarations. arab_republic_endures.description: An enduring Arab republic must demonstrate that cooperation and Iraqi independence can support one another. Productive civilian institutions and a government able to defend its own decisions would give that claim substance beyond the tenure of a single leader.

icp_congress.description: The Communist Party carries the experience of repression and years spent rebuilding its organization. A governing congress must turn that experience into a programme for public institutions, rather than allow the habits of clandestine struggle to determine every appointment.

icp_independent_strategy.description: The party now carries responsibility for governing Iraq rather than merely opposing those who do. Its committees must learn to organize national institutions without assuming that the discipline of a political movement automatically produces confidence in the state.

icp_legal_cells.description: Public party offices can reconnect the government with workers and local representatives who endured years of repression. Bringing those networks into legal public life requires accountable organizers and confidence that membership will no longer expose families to arbitrary punishment.

icp_underground.description: Clandestine organization preserved experienced cadres, but it also separated them from ordinary civilian administration. Reuniting their networks with the governing party will strengthen its reach, provided security habits do not become a substitute for professional public service.
icp_underground.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.

icp_membership.description: The party cannot govern through the incomplete lists and personal recollections that once protected its members. Dependable records will help local offices find people suited to public work without turning every administrative question into an appeal to the secretariat.
icp_membership.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.

icp_democratic_front.description: A socialist government can seek cooperation from unions, intellectuals and parties that do not accept every Communist position. Their participation would widen the republic's civilian expertise, while placing real limits on the leadership's freedom to decide alone.
icp_democratic_front.reference: IRQ_ministry_of_education/IRQ_restructure_school_curriculum (05_iraq.txt): real education law and education-cost/research spirit. 1970 adaptation uses education costs/literacy or bounded categories.
icp_democratic_front.rationale: Pluralist socialism emphasizes civilian expertise and household production rather than capped stability.

icp_vanguard.description: The party can concentrate political direction and industrial priorities in a disciplined governing apparatus. Such a state would be better placed to direct resources toward military production, but Iraqi households would bear the claims that this places on the civilian economy.
icp_vanguard.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army/IRQ_address_army_corruption (05_iraq.txt): 25 land XP/command power and native institutions. SOV_academy: planning/training institution; scaled native military modifier package.
icp_vanguard.rationale: The vanguard concentrates military-industrial production and command, while consuming more civilian resources.

icp_union_autonomy.description: Workers need representatives able to raise practical disputes without first obtaining a minister's permission. Independent unions can make production more dependable through negotiated cooperation, even where their demands reduce the output that managers would otherwise require.

icp_state_unions.description: Unions can instead be organized around the targets of the national production plan. Clear priorities would support longer and more consistent industrial runs, but workers would have fewer independent channels through which to contest those demands.
icp_state_unions.reference: IRQ_state_sponsored_industries/IRQ_revive_damaged_companies (05_iraq.txt): civilian plant delivery and +15% civilian construction spirit; no paid generic helper copied.
icp_state_unions.rationale: State unions offer plan discipline and higher production depth instead of the other model's efficiency recovery.

icp_national_question.description: The party cannot resolve Iraq's nationalities question by treating every disagreement as a class misunderstanding. A recognized charter must give communities responsibilities that the government respects, while leaving the terms of any northern settlement to those who must live with it.
icp_national_question.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
icp_national_question.rationale: A nationalities charter changes security and political vulnerability; it does not settle another actor's consent automatically.

icp_industrial_workers.description: Workers' councils need functioning industry in which to demonstrate their programme. A civilian plant in Baghdad can give them that foundation, provided technical management and workplace representation learn to work together rather than compete for every operational decision.
icp_industrial_workers.reference: IRQ_state_sponsored_industries/IRQ_revive_damaged_companies (05_iraq.txt): civilian plant delivery and +15% civilian construction spirit; no paid generic helper copied.

icp_soviet_relations.description: Relations with Soviet institutions could offer Iraqi technicians access to useful designs and instruction. Our own reception and licensing services must be able to use those opportunities, while preserving Baghdad's right to negotiate the terms of cooperation.
icp_soviet_relations.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
icp_soviet_relations.rationale: An Iraqi technical reception service can use licensed equipment; actual Soviet missions/loans still require acceptance.

icp_rural_cells.description: The rural poor will judge a socialist government by what reaches their holdings and villages. Agricultural advice and dependable credit can give party organizers a productive purpose beyond political mobilization, although promises of support must be honored in difficult seasons as well.

icp_safety_inspection.description: Workplace injuries and neglected machinery impose costs on families as well as production. Inspectors able to enforce practical standards can reduce those burdens, even where taking equipment out of service frustrates a manager's immediate output target.
icp_safety_inspection.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.

icp_cadre_schools.description: The party needs technicians and administrators who can explain how a workshop should operate, not merely who should control it. Technical schools will give experienced organizers the knowledge needed to participate in Iraq's industrial development.

icp_socialist_republic.description: A socialist republic must give its productive programme a place beyond the next party congress. Public industry can support the state and civilian life together, provided the government continues to carry the social obligations on which its authority rests.

icp_socialist_republic.rationale: Keep the strong industrial capstone and add civilian productive identity; current ICP government remains essential.

aziz_negotiated_road.description: A cabinet of allies can bring experience into government that the Communist organization cannot supply by itself. Aziz must give those ministers clear responsibilities, while accepting that cooperation requires authority to be shared as well as discussed.

aziz_opposition_road.description: The party's regional congresses can give Aziz a governing mandate extending beyond the capital. Their support will strengthen an independent national apparatus, but delegates will expect their influence over appointments and policy to survive the journey back from Baghdad.

aziz_resilient_networks.description: Years of difficult political work created networks able to find people, information and practical assistance under pressure. Bringing that experience into public institutions can broaden Iraq's options, provided informal contacts are made accountable for the responsibilities they acquire.

aziz_congress_accounts.description: Delegates cannot supervise a government whose accounts remain private to the ministries. Opening reliable public records to congress scrutiny will make revenue and services more dependable, while forcing the secretariat to defend decisions it once expected simply to announce.

aziz_federal_guarantees.description: Federal guarantees must connect the northern provinces to the services and routes on which their economy depends. Baghdad can secure cooperation by recognizing those responsibilities, but it must accept that regional institutions will retain part of the revenue they administer.
aziz_federal_guarantees.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
aziz_federal_guarantees.rationale: Federal public services reduce security/transport burdens, while reserving revenue for regional institutions.

aziz_unitary_left.description: A unitary socialist government would place collection and administration under a common national direction. It promises a clearer public account, while leaving Aziz responsible for the provincial resentment that stronger central authority can provoke.
aziz_unitary_left.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
aziz_unitary_left.rationale: A unitary left concentrates collection and administration, with continuing provincial political costs.

aziz_regional_budget.description: A regional compact will mean little to households unless schools and medical services receive dependable support. Aziz must give the provinces a budget they can use without concealing the continuing obligations that those services place on the republic.

aziz_language_rights.description: Children should not be excluded from useful instruction because the language of the classroom makes it inaccessible. Broader provision will require teachers and materials suited to the communities concerned, making language rights an educational undertaking rather than a ceremonial declaration.
aziz_language_rights.reference: IRQ_ministry_of_education/IRQ_restructure_school_curriculum (05_iraq.txt): real education law and education-cost/research spirit. 1970 adaptation uses education costs/literacy or bounded categories.
aziz_language_rights.rationale: Language access delivers direct literacy through MD's native system, with the public cost of broader provision.

aziz_soviet_distance.description: Friendship with Moscow should not require Baghdad to accept every Soviet political expectation. Maintaining room to disagree will encourage a wider range of technical and commercial relationships, although Iraq must still meet the commitments it has actually made.
aziz_soviet_distance.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
aziz_soviet_distance.rationale: Room to disagree builds resilience and diversified project administration; it does not erase Soviet contracts.

aziz_worker_training.description: A new industrial order needs workers able to master unfamiliar machinery and help others use it. Practical training can improve both factory organization and civilian production, while placing demands on the services supporting workers and their families.
aziz_worker_training.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
aziz_worker_training.rationale: Workplace training improves both production organization and the civil industrial sector.

aziz_united_opposition.description: A socialist government cannot treat every criticism as an attempt to overthrow it. Parliamentary allies and workplace representatives need a recognized means of challenging ministers without dismantling the institutions through which they must govern together.
aziz_united_opposition.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
aziz_united_opposition.rationale: Parliamentary allies become a functioning oversight institution; legal guarantees still use the existing acceptance system.

aziz_civilian_welfare.description: Military prestige will not replace medical care or dependable household services. Aziz can direct the state toward civilian welfare and a more regular military establishment, accepting the continuing public commitments that this choice entails.
aziz_civilian_welfare.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
aziz_civilian_welfare.rationale: Welfare before prestige reduces exceptional military costs and health expenditure while retaining social commitments.

aziz_workplace_delegates.description: Workplace delegates can preserve knowledge that disappears when managers reorganize a production line without consulting those who operate it. Their involvement may restrain immediate output demands, but it can make subsequent industrial work more dependable.

aziz_workplace_delegates.rationale: Delegates improve reliable production setup and long runs, at a loss of immediate forced output.

aziz_safe_return.description: Exile scattered Iraqi political experience across neighboring countries and beyond. Returning organizers should be offered useful work in reconstruction and technical instruction, while their appointments must rest on a defined public role rather than a claim to automatic authority.

aziz_rural_services.description: Villages need access to practical agricultural advice and medical assistance as well as visits from party organizers. Establishing those services will give rural government substance, but it creates obligations that Baghdad must maintain beyond a single political campaign.
aziz_rural_services.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
aziz_rural_services.rationale: Rural services combine agricultural extension and medical access, with a lasting public commitment.

aziz_party_renewal.description: A party cannot govern indefinitely through the methods that allowed it to survive in hiding. Aziz must renew its leadership and public accounts together, turning experienced organizers into an administration capable of answering for the work entrusted to it.

civic_reconstitution.description: Civilian parties must rebuild institutions that have repeatedly been displaced by military and party struggles. Their claim to govern Iraq will depend on public offices able to act predictably without relying on the personal protection of a commander.
civic_reconstitution.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
civic_reconstitution.rationale: Civilian politics establishes an actual civil administrative base, without a prerequisite that unlocks an already governing party.

civic_social_republic.description: A social republic would make public provision part of the ordinary responsibilities of government. Medical care and a stronger civilian economy can support that settlement, provided elected ministers accept the cost of commitments that survive changes of cabinet.
civic_social_republic.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
civic_social_republic.rationale: The social republic offers broad public provision and household productive capacity, with real welfare obligations.

civic_liberal_republic.description: Private undertakings need confidence that contracts and investment conditions will survive a political change in Baghdad. A liberal republic can offer that continuity, while accepting the revenue concessions required to encourage construction outside the state sector.
civic_liberal_republic.reference: IRQ_state_sponsored_industries/IRQ_revive_damaged_companies (05_iraq.txt): civilian plant delivery and +15% civilian construction spirit; no paid generic helper copied.
civic_liberal_republic.rationale: The liberal alternative offers private building/finance capacity at a tax concession; not an identical efficiency package.

civic_social_budget.description: Social rights must be supported by accounts that connect promises with the services expected to fulfill them. A civilian government can make education and care more dependable by treating their administration as permanent work rather than a succession of ministerial initiatives.
civic_social_budget.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
civic_social_budget.rationale: Social-rights accounts turn money into public services instead of global research.

civic_commercial_courts.description: Iraqi businesses cannot rely on contracts whose enforcement depends on a patron inside the ministry. Professional courts and recorded procedures will make obligations more predictable, while challenging officials who profit from uncertainty and personal intervention.
civic_commercial_courts.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
civic_commercial_courts.rationale: The sole new political native corruption-level reduction. Competent courts also improve corporate collection and project contracts; once-only permanent legal reform.

civic_electoral_register.description: Representative government needs a register that citizens and competing parties can examine with confidence. Building it will require ordinary civilian offices rather than exceptional security supervision, and no party can assume that a properly organized election guarantees its victory.
civic_electoral_register.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
civic_electoral_register.rationale: A shorter actual electoral institution has civil-service and security benefits; the genuine election remains separate and is not auto-won.

civic_federal.description: A federal constitution must give the provinces practical means to exercise the responsibilities it recognizes. Better routes and regular local services can support that settlement, while requiring Baghdad to share revenue rather than merely delegate unpaid duties.
civic_federal.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
civic_federal.rationale: Federal institutions fund connected regional services at a real central-revenue concession.

civic_unitary.description: A unitary republic can offer common rules for collection and public administration throughout Iraq. Its supporters must still explain how provincial interests will be heard when the treasury and ministries remain concentrated in the capital.
civic_unitary.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
civic_unitary.rationale: A unitary republic offers stronger unified accounts, with political bargaining costs.

civic_fiscal_federalism.description: Neither a central budget nor a regional administration can function on revenue claimed twice. An agreed fiscal settlement should clarify which public bodies collect and retain income, even where that reduces the sums immediately available to Baghdad.
civic_fiscal_federalism.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
civic_fiscal_federalism.rationale: The fiscal settlement formalizes regional sector collection rather than giving the central government free net revenue.

civic_local_accounts.description: Municipal government needs records of households, services and local economic activity that can be used beyond a mayor's personal circle. Reliable accounts will help collection and public administration without requiring every routine matter to return to a national ministry.
civic_local_accounts.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
civic_local_accounts.rationale: Municipal records improve household collection and service output; minimal audit overhead remains.

civic_security_oversight.description: Civilian authority must be able to examine the work and expenditure of the security services. Ending unnecessary exceptional operations can reduce their burden, although oversight will sometimes limit the methods through which officers have gathered information.
civic_security_oversight.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.

civic_education.description: Republican schools should prepare Iraqis to participate in public and economic life rather than serve as extensions of a cabinet's patronage. Wider basic instruction requires dependable teachers and administration that continue working when political leadership changes.
civic_education.reference: IRQ_ministry_of_education/IRQ_restructure_school_curriculum (05_iraq.txt): real education law and education-cost/research spirit. 1970 adaptation uses education costs/literacy or bounded categories.
civic_education.rationale: Republican schools deliver real direct literacy and education administration; no extra free research slot.

civic_non_alignment.description: Iraq's civilian government should be able to negotiate with several partners without becoming dependent on any one of them. Diversified commercial arrangements and stronger institutions can support that independence, while limiting the resources available for political adventures abroad.
civic_non_alignment.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
civic_non_alignment.rationale: Independent diplomacy offers resilient diversified project terms while relinquishing some own external activism.

civic_labour_bargain.description: Industrial employers and workers need a recognized way to settle disputes before they interrupt production. A labour bargain will restrain some immediate demands on the workforce, but it can support safer workplaces and a more dependable industrial rhythm.
civic_labour_bargain.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
civic_labour_bargain.rationale: Labour bargaining exchanges immediate forced output for reliable production and fewer health burdens.

civic_universities.description: Universities need room to pursue technical learning without measuring every appointment against a party's immediate political needs. More independent institutions can develop Iraqi computing expertise, provided the government funds their work and accepts conclusions it does not always welcome.

civic_credit_terms.description: A parliamentary government must explain the obligations it asks future budgets to carry. Transparent credit accounts can improve domestic finance, while leaving foreign lenders free to refuse proposals they consider insufficiently secure.

civic_union_compact.description: A durable labour agreement should preserve useful skills when plants change their products or managers. Recognized rights and responsibilities can make those transitions less disruptive, though maintaining the compact requires an administration able to enforce its terms.

civic_mandate.description: Civilian government needs a revenue system that survives the departure of a particular minister. Predictable collection and competent public offices would give elected institutions the means to govern without recreating a patronage machine at every political turn.
civic_mandate.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.

royal_charter.description: A restored crown would need a charter suited to an Iraq transformed since the fall of the monarchy. Its supporters must offer credible public contracts and protections rather than expect the old title alone to secure confidence at home or abroad.

royal_ceremonial.description: A ceremonial crown would leave the daily work of government to responsible civilian ministers. That separation can make public undertakings easier to trust, while requiring the palace to surrender much of the discretion associated with an executive monarch.
royal_ceremonial.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
royal_ceremonial.rationale: A ceremonial crown encourages predictable civilian contracts but relinquishes political discretion.

royal_executive.description: An executive crown would claim a direct role in appointments and national command. It could give the government a stronger center, but Iraq's memory of the monarchy means that concentrated royal authority will face doubts no proclamation can simply remove.

royal_parliament.description: A responsible parliament must be able to question collection and public security without being treated as an obstacle to the crown. Making it useful in ordinary government will require both the palace and the ministries to accept procedures that outlast personal relationships.

royal_council.description: The palace needs advisers able to connect military appointments and diplomatic commitments with the practical needs of Iraq. A recognized council can coordinate that work, although its members must justify an establishment that might otherwise become another circle of court patronage.
royal_council.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
royal_council.rationale: The advisory council coordinates appointments and diplomacy but sustains a larger court establishment.

royal_accounts.description: The treasury must distinguish the expenses of the crown from those of the state. Clear public accounts will strengthen collection and civilian administration, while restricting the palace's ability to resolve every obligation through an informal arrangement.

royal_accounts.rationale: Separating crown and treasury gives meaningful formal revenue rather than an abstract accounts title.

royal_land_review.description: The crown cannot settle rural grievances by pretending that Iraq's land question ended with the old monarchy. A review should make cultivation and lawful claims more secure, while recognizing the public obligations created by any promise of redress.

royal_land_review.rationale: Reviewing land claims improves agricultural contracts and productive participation, at compensation obligations.

royal_property_guarantees.description: Existing owners will be more willing to build if they believe the government will honor established contracts. Such guarantees can provide immediate economic continuity, but they will leave unresolved grievances among those who regard the present distribution of property as unjust.

royal_property_guarantees.rationale: Existing property rights offer immediate investment continuity while preserving social conflict over land.

royal_compensation.description: Competing claims to land can obstruct roads and public works as effectively as a shortage of materials. A funded tribunal should provide a usable settlement of obligations without allowing the palace to decide every case through personal favor.
royal_compensation.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
royal_compensation.rationale: A funded tribunal clarifies public rights-of-way and reduces land-dispute policing; no automatic land transfer or invented foreign compensation.

royal_rural_contracts.description: Rural development requires agreements that cultivators and public authorities can understand and enforce. Clearer contracts will support agricultural work and regular collection, provided their administration reaches beyond the offices of a few influential landholders.
royal_rural_contracts.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
royal_rural_contracts.rationale: Rural contract law improves actual agricultural output and formal collection.

royal_citizenship.description: A common crown must offer Iraq's communities more than invitations to a royal ceremony. Shared access to public institutions and instruction can support a national settlement, while limiting the informal privileges through which the palace might otherwise seek support.
royal_citizenship.reference: IRQ_ministry_of_education/IRQ_restructure_school_curriculum (05_iraq.txt): real education law and education-cost/research spirit. 1970 adaptation uses education costs/literacy or bounded categories.
royal_citizenship.rationale: A common crown builds public access and resistance to foreign interference instead of capped stability.

royal_jordan.description: Talks with Jordan could open useful commercial and military contacts between the two governments. Iraq should prepare officials able to pursue that cooperation without assuming that family connections entitle Baghdad to a treaty, federation or another country's decisions.
royal_jordan.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
royal_jordan.rationale: Iraqi commercial/military liaison teams have a direct payoff; a Jordanian treaty, federation or monarch still requires Jordanian consent.

royal_service.description: A royal civil service must be able to carry out public work without waiting for an intervention from the palace. Professional appointments and dependable administration can make the restored order more credible than a revival of old offices and titles.
royal_service.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
royal_service.rationale: An accountable professional service provides civil output and appointments.

royal_education.description: Schools can give citizenship a practical meaning for families that have little direct contact with the capital. The crown should support basic instruction through institutions that serve the public rather than requiring personal loyalty to the royal household.
royal_education.reference: IRQ_ministry_of_education/IRQ_restructure_school_curriculum (05_iraq.txt): real education law and education-cost/research spirit. 1970 adaptation uses education costs/literacy or bounded categories.
royal_education.rationale: Schools and citizenship produce direct literacy, not just a decorative crown event.

royal_commerce.description: Commercial partnership depends on the terms under which people can use Iraqi offices, contracts and investment procedures. A more practiced service will make those arrangements easier to use, while leaving private and foreign partners to decide whether they wish to invest.
royal_commerce.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
royal_commerce.rationale: Standard commercial contracts improve offices and incoming investment administration; no investor is forced to pay.

royal_public_works.description: The crown's public programme should be visible in useful routes and services. Work around Basra can support the commercial life of southern Iraq, provided the treasury meets the obligations involved instead of treating royal sponsorship as a substitute for funding.
royal_public_works.reference: PER_anti_corrupt_initiative (05_iran.txt): −10% corruption cost/+2.5% population-tax modifier; actual mapped economy fields. Scaled Iraqi institutional adaptation.
royal_public_works.rationale: One paid Basra infrastructure project anchors the public-works programme; no generic helper or extra fossil plant.

royal_budget_review.description: A regular budget should reveal whether public commitments are supported by dependable income. Parliamentary and ministerial scrutiny can improve collection and medical administration, while requiring the palace to defend priorities it might prefer to settle privately.
royal_budget_review.reference: PER_pillar_of_welfare/PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt): −5% health, −5% welfare, +5% growth/+10% efficiency gain with costs. Actual PER_economy_modifier mappings.
royal_budget_review.rationale: The budget review improves real collection and medical administration instead of a second identical treasury-account package.

royal_settlement.description: A constitutional crown can endure only if the institutions around it carry the daily work of government. A settled charter would give public and commercial partners clearer terms, while maintaining the offices needed to turn those commitments into ordinary practice.
royal_settlement.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt): −25% receiving investment duration/cost and domestic trade-offs; only Iraq-owned capability delivered here, foreign treaties remain consent-based.
royal_settlement.rationale: A constitutional settlement has a distinctive investment/sovereignty profile; −15% is a modifier, not exact calendar-day savings.

kdp_national_government.description: A KDP cabinet governing Iraq must administer a republic larger and more diverse than the movement's original northern base. Its ministers will need ordinary public offices that can serve Arab and Kurdish communities without reducing government to a succession of personal agreements.
kdp_national_government.reference: IRQ_cooperation_with_army/IRQ_restructured_police (05_iraq.txt/Iraqi.txt): root-out resistance effectiveness and police-cost reform; country effects are not a geographic security guarantee.
